title: The (Revised) Simplex Algorithm: the Gist
text:
The simplex algorithm solves linear problems in their standard form, i.e., the following type of optimization problems: \[\begin{align}
    \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} \; & c^\top x
    \\
    \text{s.t.} \; & A x = b \tag{Primal Problem}\label{eq_primal}
    \\
    & x \geq 0 \enspace,
\end{align}\] where \(c \in \mathbb{R}^n\), \(b \in \mathbb{R}^m\), and \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}\).

title: The (Revised) Simplex Algorithm: the Gist
text:
The Optimality Conditions
The Karusk-Kuhn-Tucker optimality conditions write, for \(x \in \mathbb{R}^n, \lambda \in \mathbb{R}^m, \text{and } \mu \in \mathbb{R}^n\): \[\begin{align}
    & A^\top \lambda + \mu = c \tag{KKT-1}\label{eq-KKT1}
    \\
    & Ax = b
    \\
    & x \geq 0
    \\
    & \mu \geq 0
    \\
    & x_i \mu_i = 0 , \tag{Complementary Slackness}\label{eq-complslackness}
    \enspace \text{for } i \in 1, \dots, n
    \enspace .
\end{align}\] Since the problem is convex, with linear equality and inequality constraints, the Karusk-Kuhn-Tucker conditions are necessary and sufficient for being a solution of the linear \(\ref{eq_primal}\). In other words, if one can find a triplet \((x, \lambda, \mu)\) that satisfies the KKT conditions, then \(x\) is an optimal point for the \(\ref{eq_primal}\).
